question.text: Let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo>×</mo><mn>3</mn></math> real matrices such that <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> is a symmetric matrix and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> is a skew-symmetric matrix. Then the system of linear equations <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mrow><msup><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo> </mo><msup><mi>B</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><msup><mi>B</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo> </mo><msup><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfenced><mi>X</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>O</mi><mo>,</mo></math> where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>X</mi></math> is a <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo>×</mo><mn>1</mn></math> column matrix of unknown variables and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>O</mi></math> is a <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo>×</mo><mn>1</mn></math> null matrix, has

solution.text:
Let AT=A and BT=-B

C=A2B2-B2A2

CT=A2 B2T-B2 A2T

=B2TA2T-A2TB2T

=B2 A2-A2 B2

CT=-C

C is skew symmetric.

So det C=0

so system have infinite solutions.
